points: Points played in good faith stand. When you find a mistake, fix it from now on.
Served from the wrong half: serve the next point from the correct half.
Forgot to change ends: swap ends at once.
Doubles, wrong partner serving: swap servers if the game is still on. If the game is over, follow the new order from now on.
Doubles, receivers on the wrong sides: it stays for the rest of that game. Go back the next time they receive in that set.
The server says the score out loud before every point. It prevents most score fights.
If you disagree on the score, keep the points and games you both agree on and replay only the disputed ones. You may not replay the whole set.
In a disagreement: stop at once, check whose call it was, give the benefit of the doubt, and keep everyone off court out of it.
If you cannot settle it, note what happened, finish the match, and let the captains take it to the District League Coordinator.

questions.q: At 30-15 you notice the last point was served from the wrong half of the court. What do you do?
options: The point stands. Serve the next point from the correct half
Replay the last point from the correct half
The server loses the last point
Start the game again
questions.why: Points played in good faith stand. The server serves the next point from the correct half.
questions.ref: Guide section 09, Errors made about serving or receiving

questions.q: Two points into a game, you notice you forgot to change ends after the last game. What do you do?
options: Swap ends at once. The points played stand
Finish the game, then swap ends
Swap ends and replay the two points
Stay where you are until the next odd game
questions.why: If you forgot to change ends, swap ends at once. Points already played stand.
questions.ref: Guide section 09, Errors made about serving or receiving

questions.q: Doubles. In the middle of a game you notice the wrong partner is serving. What do you do?
options: Swap servers now. The points played stand
Let that player finish the game
Replay the game with the right server
The serving team loses the game
questions.why: If the server is out of turn and the game is still on, swap servers. Points already played stand.
questions.ref: Guide section 09, Errors made about serving or receiving

questions.q: Doubles. After a game is over, you notice the wrong partner served all of it. What do you do?
options: The game stands. Follow the new order from now on
Replay the game with the right server
Go back to the old order in the next service game
The serving team loses that game
questions.why: If the game is finished, it stands, and you follow the new serving order from now on.
questions.ref: Guide section 09, Errors made about serving or receiving

questions.q: Doubles. In the middle of a game the receivers notice they are on the wrong sides, deuce and ad swapped. What do they do?
options: Stay that way for the rest of the game, then go back the next time they receive
Swap back at once
Replay the game from the start
Keep the new sides for the rest of the set
questions.why: It stays wrong for the rest of that game. The receivers go back to their sides the next time they receive in that set. Points already played stand.
questions.ref: Guide section 09, Errors made about serving or receiving

questions.q: Who says the score, and when?
options: The server, out loud, before every point
The receiver, before every point
The server, at the start of each game only
Anyone, when someone asks
questions.why: The server announces the score: the game score before the first point of a game, the point score before every other point. Out loud, every point.
questions.ref: Guide section 09, Disputes about the score

questions.q: You and your opponents do not agree on the score in a game. How do you settle it?
options: Keep the points you both agree on and replay only the disputed ones
Start the game again from love all
The server's score stands
Spin a racquet for the disputed points
questions.why: Keep all the points and games you both agree on, and replay only the disputed ones.
questions.ref: Guide section 09, Disputes about the score

questions.q: You cannot agree on the game score in a set. Can you start the whole set again?
options: No. Keep what you agree on and replay only the rest
Yes, if both sides want to
Yes, if the set was less than half done
Yes, but only once per match
questions.why: You may not replay the whole set. Keep the games you both agree on and replay only the disputed ones.
questions.ref: Guide section 09, Disputes about the score

questions.q: Something goes wrong during a point: a distraction, a ball rolling on, a wrong score. What is the first thing to do if you want to claim it?
options: Stop at once. The claim is gone if you play on
Finish the point, then raise it
Wait for the changeover to talk about it
Tell your captain after the match
questions.why: Stop at once. Any claim (hindrance, let, distraction, wrong score) is gone if you play on.
questions.ref: Guide section 09, How to handle a divergence

questions.q: You and your opponents are arguing over a line call. Your captain is watching from the side. Can you ask the captain to decide?
options: No. Nobody off court takes part
Yes, if both sides agree to ask
Yes, if the captain saw it clearly
Yes, but only the home captain
questions.why: Do not involve anyone off court: not your captain, your coach, players on another court or someone watching. The only exception is the timed procedure in the last 20 minutes.
questions.ref: Guide section 09, How to handle a divergence

questions.q: You have a real disagreement and cannot settle it on court. What do you do?
options: Note what happened, finish the match, and let the captains take it to the District League Coordinator
Stop the match and leave the court
Ask the club front desk to decide
Replay the whole match on another day
questions.why: If you cannot settle it, note what happened, finish the match, and let the captains take it to the District League Coordinator afterward.
questions.ref: Guide section 09, How to handle a divergence
